loss/p: Softmax hands back probabilities: zero point seven, zero point two and zero point one.
loss/y: The image really is class zero, so y is zero. For the loss, only that class's probability matters.
loss/L: The loss is minus the log of it. Minus the log of zero point seven is about zero point three six.
loss/wrong: Had the right class been class two, it would be minus the log of zero point one: two point three zero. Less probability on the truth, more loss.
curve/curve: Here is the loss, minus log p, for every p from zero to one.
curve/one: At p equal to one, a confident right answer, the loss is zero. It never dips below zero, because the log of a probability is never positive.
curve/zero: As p falls toward zero, the loss climbs without limit. A confident wrong answer costs the most.
scores/s: From scores, softmax makes p of y equal to e to the right score, over the total, T.
scores/rule: Take minus the log, and the loss is the log of the total, minus the right class's score. For scores two, one and minus one, with y equal to zero, that is two point three five minus two: zero point three five.
scores/init: Before training, the scores are about equal, so each of C classes gets one over C, and the loss is log C. With ten classes, two point three zero.
example/ask: Your turn. The probabilities are zero point one, zero point six and zero point three, and the right class is two. The log of zero point three is about minus one point two zero.
example/pick: The loss looks only at class two, with zero point three. Not zero point six, even though that is the largest.
example/L: Minus its log, minus minus one point two zero, gives a loss of one point two zero.
